correctness.rationale: For any monotone self-map of a finite poset, a point comparable with its image generates a monotone iterate chain that stabilizes at a fixed point. Hence a fixed-point-free map in the stated class must send every point to its unique incomparable mate. This makes the map a fixed-point-free involution. Monotonicity of the involution forces all cross-comparisons between two mate pairs to have one uniform direction, so the mate pairs are totally ordered and the poset is an ordinal sum of two-point antichains. The converse is direct. The cross-polytope degree is the determinant sign of central inversion. A dependency-free exhaustive checker verifies all labeled posets on at most four points and the first three canonical models.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural and exact boundary: among finite spaces whose incomparability graph has maximum degree one, the only spaces failing the fixed point property are the canonical minimal sphere models, and their fixed-point-free map is forced and unique. This converts a local order constraint into a global topological classification and links finite-space fixed-point theory to extremal sphere models. The result is symbolic for all cardinalities; the finite enumeration is only a stress test.
